la:noun:adamas.gloss: Adamant; the hardest steel or iron; diamond; an object made of adamant.
senses: Adamant; the hardest steel or iron; diamond; an object made of adamant.
Anything which is inflexible, firm or lasting.
Hard, invincible, unconquerable, unyielding, inexorable, stubborn, intractable.
la:noun:adamas.html:
ădămas, antis, m. (acc. Gr. adamanta, adamantas), = ἀδάμας (invincible),
adamant, the hard est iron or steel; hence poet., for any thing inflexible, firm, lasting, etc. (first used by Verg.): porta adversa ingens solidoque adamante columnae,; cf. ; adamante texto vincire,with adamantine chains,.—Trop. of character, hard, unyielding, inexorable: nec rigidos silices solidumve in pectore ferrum aut adamanta gerit,a heart of stone,: lacrimis adamanta movebis,will move a heart of stone,; so : voce tua posses adamanta movere,: duro nec enim ex adamante creati, Sed tua turba sumus,. —
The diamond: adamanta infragilem omni cetera vi sanguine hireino rumpente, 37, 4, 15, § 55 sq.

senses: a male given name, equivalent to English Adam

la:verb:adaequo.gloss: to make equal to, equalize, level with
senses: to make equal to, equalize, level with
to attain to, reach by equalling
la:verb:adaequo.html:
ăd-aequo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.
Act.
To make equal to, to equalize, to level with; hence,
In Cic. usually with cum (cf. aequare cum, ): qui cum virtute fortunam adaequavit,: quae ... admonet, commemorationem nominis nostri, cum omni posteritate adaequandam,: in summa amicorum copia cum familiarissimis ejus est adaequatus (i. e. par habitus),.—
In the histt. alicui rei (cf.: aequo and aequiparo): molibus ferme (oppidi) moenibus adaequatis,on a level with,: omnia tecta solo adaequare,to level with the ground,: quibus duobus operibus vix nova haec magnificentia quidquam adaequare potuit,; and with solo understood: Alesiam flammis adaequare,: cum Claudius libertos sibique et legibus adaequaverit,: colonias jure et dignatione urbi ... adaequavit,; so Dom. 2.—
Trop., to compare to or with: qui formam, aetatem, genus mortis magni Alexandri fatis adaequarent,.—
To attain to, or reach, by equalling. —With acc. (cf.: aequo and aequiparo): ne quid absit quod deorum vitam possit adaequare,: longarum navium cursum adaequaverunt,: ut muri altitudinem acervi armorum adaequarent,; cf. , and .
Neut., to be equal.
Absol.: senatorum urna copiose absolvit, equitum adaequavit, the votes of the equites were equally divided, there was an equal number for acquitting and for condemning, .—
With dat.: turris quae moenibus adaequaret, Auct. B. G. 8, 41: se virtute nostris adaequare non posse intellegunt, Dinter, where some read nostros: adaequare apud Caesarem gratiā, sc. Aeduis, id. B: G. 6, 12.
la:verb:adaequo.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. and n.

la:verb:adaugeo.gloss: to make greater by adding to; increase, augment; magnify
senses: to make greater by adding to; increase, augment; magnify
la:verb:adaugeo.html:
ăd-augĕo, xi, ctum, 2, v. a.,
to make greater by adding to, to increase, augment.
In gen.: timet, ne tua duritia adaucta sit,: haec maleficia aliis nefariis cumulant atque adaugent,; so ; ; cf. ; ; ; —
Esp., in sacrifices, t. t., to devote (cf. augeo): decumam esse adauctam tibi quam vovi,.

la:verb:adaugesco.html:
ăd-augesco, ĕre,
v. inch. n. [ad, intens.], to begin to increase or augment, to grow, to thrive: neque adaugescit quidquam neque deperit inde,; so also Cic. poet. in Div. 1, 7 fin.
